transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-01
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (CTO - Synthex), Priya Rao (Lead ML Eng), Samir Gupta (Platform Eng)

Summary:
- Integration discovery focused on Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Synthex's customer-facing assistant.
- Key topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex patterns, gateway/proxy integration, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC).
- Agreed next step: send integration guide + schedule infra deep dive.

Topics:
- SDKs & quickstarts
- LangChain/LlamaIndex examples
- Gateway/proxy and auth flow
- Rate limiting and quotas (burst vs steady)
- Observability/tracing hooks and cost breakdowns
- Deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, joining with riya our se, we'll keep this pretty focused on how you'd actually integrate — quick intro from you and then we can go into the SDK bits and infra.
[00:18] Jordan (Synthex): hey alex, jordan here, CTO; priya and samir are on, we run the assistant that's customer-facing — about 3m monthly active users, peaks around 2k rps internally on the front end, but the assistant traffic is spikey, so curious about burst behavior.
[00:36] Priya (Synthex): yeah real quick, our stack is node/python services, main convo flow goes through a gateway that does auth and rate-limiting, we use LangChain for orchestration today with some LlamaIndex retrieval.
[00:50] Riya (Redwood SE): great, that matches what we usually see; we have official SDKs for python and node, and examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns. I'll share snippets after the call.
[01:10] Samir (Synthex): small note — we have a central proxy (kong-based) that enforces quotas and per-tenant limits; we'd rather not expose raw api keys, so interested in gateway/proxy auth patterns.
[01:30] Alex: totally, two common patterns: 1) server-side calls through your gateway using a Redwood service token stored in KMS, or 2) token broker in your infra that mints short-lived keys. Both supported — for Dedicated/Private we also do VPC peering.
[02:05] Priya: can you remind us how rate limits are surfaced? we have bursty diurnal patterns and need per-tenant quotas.
[02:20] Riya: Hosted API has rate-limit headers and quota controls per api key, but for multi-tenant staff you'd typically front it with your proxy and enforce tenant quotas there; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput, with ability to set per-route limits.
[02:45] Jordan: ok, and what about latency vs cost tradeoffs? our SLO is 400ms p95 for short prompt completions.
[03:00] Riya: p95 is feasible on Hosted for small models depending on region; Dedicated reduces variance and routing hops, plus you can pin model variants and quantization. Also batching affects p95 — small batch sizes for sub-100ms adds overhead.
[03:25] Alex: we can run a bench for your prompt profile — a light benchmark spreadsheet works well, we'll ask for sample prompts and token distributions.
[03:40] Priya: awesome, we'll put together a representative prompt set.
[04:05] Samir: question on observability — we need per-request tracing + token-level cost attribution, and hooks into our datadog.
[04:20] Riya: we expose request metadata and tracing hooks; you can pass a request_id through x-request-id header and we surface token counts, latency, and model used. We also have webhooks and a tempo/tracing exporter for OTEL.
[04:50] Jordan: does that include KV/prefix cache visibility? we do a lot of retrieval-augmented flows and cache hit rates matter.
[05:05] Riya: yes — for prefix/KV caching we emit cache-hit/miss metrics and per-route cache stats in the console; on Dedicated you can tune cache sharing policies.
[05:30] Alex: quick aside — when you use LangChain or LlamaIndex, you can swap in our SDK client; we've got a couple of recipe repos. There are some common mis-steps — e.g., naive retries cause token duplication and cost spikes, we'll share guidance.
[06:00] Priya: nice, we saw cost regressions when retries stacked during a regional blip. What about automatic fallback to smaller models for graceful degradation?
[06:20] Riya: supported — smart routing policies let you fallback to a cheaper model family, or route to Dedicated fallback pool. That helps preserve latency SLOs while lowering cost during high load.
[06:45] Jordan: security: soc2, encryption, can we bring our own KMS?
[06:58] Alex: yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Hosted we provide envelope encryption and support customer keys via KMS integration in enterprise tiers. We'll send SOC2 and network diagrams.
[07:20] Samir: for private, is there an on-prem box or is it VPC-only?
[07:30] Riya: both options: VPC control plane and a private deployment package that can run in your datacenter; hybrid patterns exist. We'll include docs.
[08:10] Priya: can we see an example of the gateway pattern? so the flow would be frontend -> our gateway -> redwood (or dedicated) ?
[08:25] Alex: yes, the typical flow: frontend authenticated -> your backend/gateway -> call Redwood with a service token (or short-lived token broker) -> Redwood returns streaming tokens if you want streaming. For streaming you need to keep an open connection; we support SSE and chunked HTTP.
[08:55] Jordan: about streaming — our UI wants partial tokens for progressive render, is that mature on your side?
[09:10] Riya: streaming is production-grade; we do function/tool calling and structured outputs too. Note that streaming slightly changes how you account tokens, we break out prompt vs generation.
[09:35] Priya: we heavily use LangChain chains with retrievers; any gotchas integrating LlamaIndex?
[09:50] Riya: LlamaIndex integrations are common; watch for idempotency in your retriever calls, and ensure you pass context windows and KV cache hints. We'll share a LlamaIndex snippet — there's a sample repo.
[10:15] Samir: can we set different quotas per model family? e.g., cheaper model for normals, larger model for admin queries.
[10:30] Alex: yep, per-route and per-model quotas and routing rules are supported; you can implement canary rollouts and auto-fallback in the console.
[11:00] Jordan: curious about SDK latency overhead vs raw REST.
[11:10] Riya: SDK is a thin wrapper; raw REST is similar performance, sdk mainly helps with auth, retries, and streaming helpers.
[11:30] Priya: about retries — what's your recommendation to avoid duplicate tokens?
[11:40] Riya: idempotency keys on requests are important; we support idempotency keys for the generation endpoints. Also prefer client-side circuit breakers and backoff.
[12:05] Alex: let's talk traffic shaping; Samir you mentioned a kong proxy — any constraints for TTL or caching?
[12:20] Samir: we already do per-tenant buckets and have a burst buffer; we want Redwood to accept token usage headers so we can attribute cost back to tenants.
[12:35] Riya: we provide token usage in the response and via metrics export; you can pipe that into your billing pipeline.
[13:00] Jordan: procurement questions — what does the contract look like for Dedicated?
[13:10] Alex: Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit, SLA for uptime and latency tiers; pricing is a mix of commit + overage. We'll send a sample term sheet.
[13:40] Priya: and for PII data retention / redaction?
[13:50] Alex: we support configurable retention and can enable automated redaction patterns; for Private deployments you retain full control.
[14:10] Samir: can we run a POC — say two-week smoke with traffic replay?
[14:22] Riya: absolutely, common approach is a pilot on Hosted with constrained quotas or a small Dedicated pool. We'll help with a benchmark harness.
[14:40] Jordan: what telemetry do you surface to datadog? traces, metrics?
[14:52] Riya: traces (OTEL), metrics (token counts, latency buckets, cache hit/miss), logs (request-level) via secure forwarding or webhook.
[15:10] Priya: ok let's dive a little deeper into the LangChain pattern — we orchestrate multiple retrievers and a reasoning chain, sometimes we need to pin a conversation's model mid-flight.
[15:30] Riya: you can pin model via the request param; for multi-step flows we surface the kv-cache handle so you can reuse context without re-sending the full prefix.
[15:55] Alex: small caveat — while kv cache reduces tokens, it can expand memory usage on dedicated pods; we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[16:20] Samir: about rate-limit headers again — are they per-key or per-account?
[16:30] Riya: both; hosted: per-key headers and account-level quotas; on Dedicated you can surface per-tenant quotas if you forward tenant id.
[16:50] Jordan: do you support SAML SSO for console access and RBAC?
[17:00] Alex: yes SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC; enterprise plans include SCIM provisioning.
[17:25] Priya: when you talk about fallback models, are they usually smaller open models?
[17:35] Riya: often yes, or compressed quantized variants; we also offer Redwood-curated families that match behaviour.
[17:55] Jordan: any known issues integrating LlamaIndex vector store vs our in-house store?
[18:10] Riya: compatibility is generally fine, main thing is embedding vector format — we support common formats; we also provide embeddings endpoints or you can bring your own.
[18:40] Samir: we want to avoid exposing raw embeddings in transit, any encryption in flight?
[18:50] Alex: TLS in transit and mTLS optional for Private; encrypt at rest with KMS.
[19:10] Priya: about observability hooks — can we annotate spans with user_id and tenant_id?
[19:25] Riya: yes, pass them as headers and they'll be attached to traces (PII considerations apply).
[19:45] Jordan: how granular is token accounting — per-request, per-route, per-model?
[19:55] Riya: per-request is default, and we aggregate per-route and per-model for the console and exports.
[20:20] Alex: quick check — any blockers from security/legal for Hosted?
[20:30] Samir: need SOC2 plus KMS options; data residency may be an issue for eu customers.
[20:45] Alex: we have region options and Private for residency. we'll share the compliance pack.
[21:05] Priya: what's the typical onboarding time for Dedicated?
[21:15] Riya: Dedicated can be days to a few weeks depending on networking (VPC peering) and quota sizing; Private on-prem can be longer.
[21:35] Jordan: demo request — want to see LangChain sample and streaming in action.
[21:45] Alex: we'll schedule a short demo and a deeper technical session.
[22:05] Riya: i'll prepare a small repo with LangChain and LlamaIndex samples, plus a benchmark harness we can run against your prompts.
[22:30] Samir: we'll prepare a traffic replay and sample prompt set; also share our kong config.
[22:50] Alex: next steps recap — i'll send integration guide, pricing/term sheet, and SOC2 + network diagrams, riya will send code samples, samir to share gateway details.
[23:10] Jordan: sounds good, thanks.
[23:20] Priya: thanks all.
[23:30] Alex: closing — expect the docs in 24-48h and we'll lock demo time.

(Notes: transcript has been lightly cleaned but retains some disfluencies and occasional misheard tokens)
